notes: The operator: PoTS becomes "a first-class DESIGN objective rather than only a business metric" — "How much operator time did this constitutional workflow save without creating additional repair burden?" That is a measurement question, and it is open.
question: Can Time to Value and Time to Repair be MEASURED per workflow rather than argued about — and should a constitutional workflow carry its own TTV/TTR budget?
context: The operator ratified the TTV/TTR objective as a design rule and named measurable dimensions for both. The platform already computes Net Value Acceleration at outcome time from claimed hours. The open question is whether design-time TTV/TTR can be instrumented rather than estimated.
wouldRequire: An instrument: the TTV dimensions the operator named (clicks, navigation, decisions, elapsed time, interruptions, operator interventions) are observable in principle, but nothing measures them today.
A decision on whether a measured TTV feeds PoTS directly, given PoTS accrues to Standing only after verification — an automatically measured input to a verification-gated metric needs its own gate.
A baseline. Without one, "materially reduces Time to Value" stays a judgement, which is what the two questions in the ratified principle currently are.
